reviews.title: Game changer
reviews.contents:
This app was a game changer for my four month old daughter’s sleep. She was one of those babies who would take half an hour of rocking and wake as soon as we put her down. So she’d end up having most of her naps on me. She would feed to sleep at night and sleep pretty well in her cot usually so we weren’t too bothered about changing anything. But then at around the four month mark she would wake at night every two hours and insist on being held. This is when we enlisted the help of this app. 

We tried to follow the routines as closely as possible but this was difficult as our little girl is both an early riser and a cat napper. Resettling had never worked for her. I may have said “this is bull####, what a waste of money” to my husband on the first morning. But I persisted and on that very first day she had a two hour nap (with a resettle after half an hour).

After a couple of weeks she is so much easier to put down for sleeps. And a great part of this app is that you can use as much of the advice as you’d like. We don’t follow the routines religiously (eg. if she wants to nap for longer than the suggested time in the morning we don’t wake her, although we do in the afternoon). We mostly work on awake time. I would recommend this app to anyone struggling with a bub like mine.

reviews.title: New update has taken away useful features
reviews.contents:
Hi there. 
Not normally one to write reviews but hoping this review helps restore some of the features taken away with the most recent update. 

I have loved little ones since I've been using it (my little one is almost 5 months & we’ve been using it since we got home from hospital). 

However, the most recent update claims to give us ‘new resettling feature’ when I reality it has taken away way more useful features within the app. 

Ie. if I forgot to start my sleep timer I could edit the start time… now I can not 

If I forgot to hit stop on a feed l…I could edit the length of the feed. Now I’m unable to get the time to go below 1 hour if I need to edit it. 

Sure I could remember to start and stop the app. But let’s face it sometimes when you’re handling your little one, these things get forgotten. 

Also there is no way to distinguish a nap versus overnight sleep? Which doesn’t make sense considering the plans also give you an indication of ideal nap amounts each day. So now you’d have to manually work out how much nap time you’ve had compared to before when able would tell you the accumulated amount based on you choosing what kind of sleep it is. 

Really hoping these features are restored asap. As really the resettling info was fine before when you could hit stop and resume & it would log it for you. 

Hopefully someone is going through usability as it’s really taken the app backwards.

Kind regards,
Little ones fan (I swear) :)

reviews.title: It’s not a gimmick!
reviews.contents: This program has been an absolute life saver for our family. Our son who is now 5 months, really struggled to settle once his sleep cycles changed at 3.5months. We were using a dummy to settle, sometimes hourly overnight. We felt like zombies! I was sceptical about the program because I was worried about following a “schedule”, but it has been exactly what my son needed. We saw improvements from day one! We ditched the dummy and started working on self settling all at once and by his lunch time nap on the first day, we were settling and sleeping through! It’s been 6 days now and our son sleeps 7pm - 7am with one to two feeds. He doesn’t protest naps anymore and we now have our evenings to ourselves again…and our room! I would 100% recommend this program. I had no idea that just making small adjustments like following awake times could make such a huge difference to our sons sleep. Worth every dollar!

reviews.title: Love this app
reviews.contents: I started using this app with my second born and wish I’d known about it for my first. Being new to parenting, I remember everyone asking if I’d gotten Bub in to a routine yet but I had absolutely no idea how to do that. With my second, I happened to stumble across the app and decided to give it a go. She was already around 6 months old I think at the time and it took a bit of work and a couple of sometimes challenging weeks, but once we got her on track, it was a game changer. It just really took a lot of the guesswork out - I knew she had the right amount of sleep, so I could put any fussiness down to discomfort or hunger. When I had my twins, I started them on it from early on and it has been a godsend. I recommend it to everyone. It can be hard to work around a sleep schedule but honestly, I think it’s the better option.

reviews.title: An essential!!
reviews.contents: I never write reviews. I’ve tried other sleep programs and nothing compares to this. The Little Ones app has made being a first time Mum really reassuring for sleep. There is SO much information to be able to read and different approaches to take. Having the specific awake times per age/week of baby sets it apart in my opinion. I love the village posts. I have always been able to find my answers in the middle of the night using the search bar. So good when you just want an immediate answer/solution to try. I also love that the sleep consultants can also respond to your questions within 24 hours. I have recommended this app to all of my friends and will continue to. Well done on creating an amazing resource and empowering parents!

reviews.title: Game changer!!
reviews.contents:
Yesterday we started the sleep program for our 3 month old to help with his day time naps because he would only catnap during the day in his bassinet for like 15 minutes and only have long naps on me. Which is fine, I love a contact nap, but I also like to be able to eat and shower and go to the toilet. He had no problem with sleeping at night, but I think he was probably just so exhausted and so was I 😅

We worked on his day time naps, wake windows, sleep associations and him learning how to resettle himself to be able to link his sleep cycles and he slept for 11.5 hours last night with only one quick feed at 3:50am this morning!! 

My partner and I both have ADHD and are of course first time parents so there has definitely been challenges even after trying to follow a lot of different advice online. Being able to now follow a routine as close as possible and having more structure in our day has already shown improvements for our little one even after 1 day!

I love how thorough it is and it takes a lot of the guesswork out, plus provides lots of resources and techniques all in one place! I don’t write reviews ever, but this has been a game changer already!!

reviews.title: Suggestion :)
reviews.contents:
We still aren’t getting much sleep but I see the benefits already and am excited to see night sleep fall into place now we mostly have naps down pat.
With the new feature of tracking sleep interruptions, it would be good to have these listed with times so you could see when bub woke for a feed vs a resettle overnight, and if there is any pattern to their waking/resettling as this would be really helpful for breastfed babies and their feeding patterns.
I paid for the village access and have been disappointed. It’s marketed as access to sleep consultants but in reality, it’s just you asking a question and them replying hours later with generic info that can be found in the app. It then asks you to post a new question if you’re still unsure, so it’s not really direct back and forth help which is what I needed at the time.

reviews.title: Wouldn’t recommend
reviews.contents:
Been trying this program/app for 4 months now with no real progress or change in our 1.5 year olds sleep. I appreciate the variety of options in the app depending on where you’re starting (feeding to sleep, rocking to sleep etc.) and how you want to go about it. But I found the advice wasn’t anything I hadn’t read/tried before and I didn’t find the troubleshooting notes helpful more than once. 

It’s annoying that if you want any help with the program or have questions you’re directed to the Village which is extra money. Also the sleep tracking feature of the app was almost useless - I don’t know how many times it’s told me ‘you’ve logged a sleep outside of apps capabilities’ (like YEA OBVIOUSLY, it’s taking me an hour and a half to get my toddler to sleep so she didn’t end up falling asleep in the window you set, that’s why I purchased this sleep help program 🤦🏻‍♀️). Overall, wouldn’t recommend and wish I hadn’t purchased.

reviews.title: User friendly
reviews.contents:
I like the app, I don’t love it. The colours are just not very distinctive or cohesive to what they represent. When you’re tired and getting used to the app, it took some time. & it’s just not very efficient. I don’t get why everything is a soft shade, and lots of pink when you’re trying to navigate it. I think a change in colours would be a really good move. If I have another baby, I’ll most likely spend money on another app that’s more user friendly. The recent update for sleep times with no option for nap and overnight, I’m not a fan of either. I’ve actually missed a few night logs on accident. 
Also I don’t think it was clearly stated that when you pay for it, you have to subscribe to get the village features. Which I’m not convinced to buy either due to the functionality. 
Thank you :)

reviews.title: Pros and cons
reviews.contents:
Having obsessed over 2 kids with sleep issues, I think this is a good sleep program- it’s comprehensive. My baby needed more sleep than the schedule suggested so I always went on a schedule for a baby a few months younger and just followed loosely.
But the village/ support side of this app is terrible in my opinion. There is no way to search terms- you end up having to scroll through from most recent post, read the post, realise it’s not answering your question, read the next one etc. the most reason posts are obviously also the least likely to have been answered or the discussion is unfinished so it’s very unhelpful. The Facebook village was useful because most the time you would find your answer, plus more, by searching terms and not have to ask the question yourself. I think the app is a big step back compared with the Facebook village,  and a proper search function needs to be added.
